A custom state machine ensures predictable, deterministic step-by-step task executions without the massive footprint (e.g., LangChain dependencies) associated with graph frameworks.\\n- *Why not a Graph Library?* While graph libraries (like LangGraph.js) offer powerful built-in cycles and observability, they introduce significant bundle bloat and complexity. Research Findings: Technical Mechanisms\n\n> Updated via Round 1 research mandate on path linking methodologies for the Antigravity plugin.\n\n**Path Linking Mechanism (Graph Library vs. Custom State Machine):**\nFor an IDE extension like the Antigravity plugin, a **Custom State Machine** is the most adapted mechanism. \n- *Why Custom State Machine?* IDE plugins require strict dependency constraints, minimal overhead, and small bundle sizes to remain performant. A custom state machine ensures predictable, deterministic step-by-step task executions without the massive footprint (e.g., LangChain dependencies) associated with graph frameworks.\n- *Why not a Graph Library?* While graph libraries (like LangGraph.js) offer powerful built-in cycles and observability, they introduce significant bundle bloat and complexity. Research Findings: Dynamic Context Injection\n\n> Updated via Round 2 research mandate on dynamically injecting fragmented markdown skills into the agent context.\n\n**Dynamic Injection Mechanism for Fragmented Skills:**\nFragmented skills must be formatted as Markdown (`.md`) files. To dynamically inject them into the agent context, the Devio Orchestration Engine (`prompt-builder.ts`) must dynamically resolve the path of the relevant fragmented skill (based on the current state machine step or task). The engine will then simply append `Context: @${fragmentedSkillAbsolutePath}` to the generated prompt string. The Antigravity IDE natively intercepts the `@absolute_path` syntax within the chat input via `injectMessage` and automatically embeds the file's content into the LLM context. This native resolution completely bypasses the need for complex CDP file uploads or UI interactions.\n\n## 9. Global Orchestration Design & Constraints\n\n> Deep-dive research addressing client feedback on system orchestration, workflow, and professional coding standards.\n\n**1. How the whole system will work:**\nThe system operates on a **Custom State Machine** to manage the agency's lifecycle phases (Brief, Proposal, Architecture, Development, Review, Delivery, Done). The Orchestration Engine governs state transitions based on structured agent messages (`SUBMIT`, `APPROVE`, `REQUEST_CHANGE`).
